referenced_urls.title: Stratum: Repository Memory for Coding Agents Beyond the Context Window

relevance: Repo-level memory design for long-running coding agents.

media.description: Abstract excerpt arguing coding agents need persistent, experience-aware repository memory; KV-cache storage costs 10^4–10^5x more bytes than indexed text, and median bug fixes touch two files.
media.ocr_text: Context windows have grown a thousand-fold, yet coding agents still start every session with no memory of their past work. They re-read files, retry failed approaches, and forget root causes they established hours earlier. This is not a context-length problem but a memory-architecture problem. Our hypothesis: coding agents need persistent, experience-aware repository memory, so that knowledge survives from one session to the next. Three measurements on real repositories motivate the design. First, mid-size projects already exceed the largest production context windows, and storing knowledge inside the model's key-value (KV) cache costs 10⁴ to 10⁵ times more bytes than storing it as indexed text.
